title: Wrong Together: Shared Bias in User Simulation
abstract: arXiv:2611.01354v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: User simulators generate responses in place of human participants, allowing researchers to estimate the result of a study. To use these estimates before collecting human responses, researchers need a way to assess their reliability. We test whether disagreement among simulators can identify unreliable estimates of a group's response proportions and of differences between groups. We evaluate this signal using 6 language-model simulators and existing GlobalOpinionQA responses for 60 questions in 12 countries. Disagreement predicts invalidity more accurately for differences between two groups than for a single group's response proportions (AUC 0.87 versus 0.71). Errors shared by the simulators remain invisible to this signal. When such an error affects both groups equally, it cancels in the comparison, helping explain the stronger result for group differences. translated_title: 共同犯错：用户模拟中的共享偏见
translated_abstract: 用户模拟器代替人类参与者生成回答，使研究人员能够预先估计研究结果。为了在收集人类回答之前使用这些估计，研究人员需要一种评估其可靠性的方法。我们测试了模拟器之间的分歧能否识别出不可靠的估计，包括单个群体回答比例的估计以及群体间差异的估计。我们使用6个语言模型模拟器以及现有的GlobalOpinionQA数据（涵盖12个国家的60个问题）来评估这一信号。结果表明，分歧在预测两个群体间差异的无效性方面比预测单个群体回答比例的无效性更为准确（AUC分别为0.87和0.71）。模拟器共同犯下的错误对该信号而言是不可见的。当这类错误以相同方式影响两个群体时，它会在群体比较中相互抵消，这有助于解释群体差异上更强的预测效果。我们通过使用一组群体估计共享偏见来验证这一解释。
tldr: 该研究发现模拟器之间的分歧可以作为识别不可靠估计的信号（对群体间差异的预测效果更好，AUC达0.87），但模拟器共享的偏见对该信号不可见，不过当共享错误同等地影响两个被比较的群体时会在比较中相互抵消。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that disagreement among user simulators serves as a signal for identifying unreliable estimates—working better for group differences (AUC 0.87) than for single-group response proportions—while shared bias among simulators remains invisible to this signal, though it cancels out in comparisons when it equally affects both groups.
